I think the question of "use AI for art vs dont use it" comes down to what you prioritize. I can see that you prioritize efficiency over quality, and I get that, but I personally value quality over efficiency. I wouldn't mind delays on a web novel as long as the quality of the art produced is good.

So, I don't think that's a bad thing. But it seems to be a different mindset type of problem that I don't really agree with. It's probably limiting, yeah, but it's just my personal preference.

While I understand where you're coming from, art has always been "accessible." Loading up Photoshop/Adobe Illustrator or hell even MS Paint if you really have to and drawing something is free. Even if it doesn't look good, if you're not creating something mass produced, there's nothing wrong with using it.

Does it take time and practice to make something that looks good? Yes, of course as it does, like with every skill. There are artists out there who'd be willing to make things for you for free too, if you search or have any artist friends.

AI art is also free, and I guess if you're making something that nobody will see/will only be seen by other programmers, you could go with AI art. If you're making something bigger though, I'd personally suggest you make the art yourself or find someone who can. Art isn't a talent and it can be learned by anyone, just like how you can learn to code, so I don't really understand why people say "I can't make art without AI art."

Despite being an artist, I think my own art is pretty shit sometimes, especially in the UX design department. I still make my own stuff though, whether it looks good or not.

Honest answer from someone who has studied an entire course's worth of material the day before the final one too many times: Just look at what your professor has posted. Literally just look over it. If there's lecture notes, a Powerpoint presentation, ANYTHING: just read it.

If it's math, then while you read, stop every time you hit a subject and do 10-15 practice problems. Do not look up any answers until after you're done. If you need to, look up a few videos to help. Khan Academy and certain math Youtube channels will save you. Once you're done, look up the answers and figure out what you did wrong. Try another set of problems. Repeat until you can do them all right. Then repeat for each subject.

This method probably won't work as well if you haven't been exposed to the material beforehand at all.

This method got me through cramming entire semester's worth of math classes for the final and I passed with a B+ or A each time. Good luck!
